name: Peru
headline: Peru: +3.4% growth in 2025, 1.5% inflation, debt 30% of GDP
sections: Peru is a $342 billion economy (2025), the world's 48th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.4% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $19K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 12.2% of GDP (2024).
Consumer prices rose 1.5% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 7.9% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 5.9% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 9.5% (2025).
Gross government debt is 30% of GDP (2025), a low level that has fallen from 34% in 2020. The general government balance is −2.4% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is +3.5% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 52% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 3.1% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 30% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 77.9 years (2024). Population: 34.4 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
